title: add CI artifact signing, build provenance, and release manifests for private-installer
author: Marcus Chen
description: Adds end-to-end release automation for the private-installer artifacts: builds, SBOM generation, cosign signing, provenance attestations, and canonical release-manifests used by downstream installers and air-gapped customers. Motivation: customers deploying Redwood Private require verifiable release artifacts (signed binaries, SBOMs, and provenance) and a stable release-manifests feed for offline installs and upgrades. This PR wires the CI and release tooling to produce those artifacts and publish them to our release bucket, and updates the installer chart references to consume the manifest set. Changes include: GHA workflows to build and sign artifacts, syft-based SBOM generation, cosign attestation for provenance, a small Go tool to render release-manifests (yaml/json) from release metadata, and CI gating checks that validate signatures and SBOM completeness. Checklist: - [x] build pipeline for tarballs/docker images - [x] generate SBOM (syft) and attach to artifact - [x] sign artifacts and attestations with cosign - [x] generate release-manifests and upload to release bucket - [x] update installer helm chart to reference manifest URLs - [x] add verification job to release CI - [x] documentation for operators (ci/cosign/README.md) Rollout plan: land on main behind feature flag, run release candidate job to create a manifest for the 2025.11.0 RC, validate canary installs in staging, then flip the release automation to publish stable manifests. Security notes: private key usage is gate-kept by the release runner; signing keys are held in KMS and only available to the release job. For air-gapped customers we still emit a signed set of artifacts and a release-manifests tarball customers can download via the support flow. See linked Linear tickets for acceptance tests and QA steps.
